<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915585_theRebbe_828" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915585_theRebbe_828__p004">
  <section v="9">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the three interpretations of "teva" (nature) correspond to three distinct concepts: nature as continuous miracles, as the divine life-force animating the world, and as the power that creates ex nihilo beyond intellect.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And it is explained in the discourses,</t>
    <t s="1">that the three aforementioned interpretations are three distinct matters.</t>
    <t s="2">For according to the interpretation of the Chacham Tzvi that nature is continuous miracles,</t>
    <t s="3">there the term "nature" refers to the conduct of the world.</t>
    <t s="4">And according to the interpretation that "teva" is from the term "matbea" (coin), that the Holy One, blessed be He, imprinted every person with the seal of Adam HaRishon,</t>
    <t s="5">and the Rambam explained</t>
    <t s="6">that the seal of Adam HaRishon is the form of the human species by which a human is human,</t>
    <t s="7">that the intention of "form of the human species" is</t>
    <t s="8">(primarily)</t>
    <t s="9">the spiritual form within him—</t>
    <t s="10">there the term "nature" refers to the divine life-force within the world,</t>
    <t s="11">which is the soul of the world.</t>
    <t s="12">And the connection of this matter to nature in its simple sense is,</t>
    <t s="13">that the form and nature of every created being is according to the manner of the divine life-force within it.</t>
    <t s="14">And according to the interpretation that "teva" is a borrowed term for anything not based on reason and intellect—there the term "nature" refers to the divine power that brings every created being into existence from nothing to something,</t>
    <t s="15">for bringing into existence from nothing to something is beyond intellect.</t>
    <t s="16">For this, that the divine life-force animates the created beings,</t>
    <t s="17">has a place in intellect,</t>
    <t s="18">and the matter of nature</t>
    <t s="19">(according to the interpretation that nature is that which is not based on reason and intellect)</t>
    <t s="20">is in the bringing into existence of created beings,</t>
    <t s="21">for creation of something from nothing is beyond intellect.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="10">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the two interpretations of nature—as the divine life-force and as the creative power—both relate to the meaning of "teva" as immersion, since the divine power is concealed within creation.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">6)</t>
    <t s="1">And it is explained in the discourses,</t>
    <t s="2">that the two interpretations</t>
    <t s="3">(the matters)</t>
    <t s="4">of nature,</t>
    <t s="5">that it is the divine life-force that animates the created beings and that it is the divine power that brings the created beings into existence from nothing to something,</t>
    <t s="6">are related to the interpretation that "teva" is from the term "teviah" (immersion),</t>
    <t s="7">"they sank"</t>
    <t s="8">in the Sea of Reeds.</t>
    <t s="9">For just as in simple immersion,</t>
    <t s="10">when something is immersed in water,</t>
    <t s="11">the water covers the thing immersed in them,</t>
    <t s="12">so too is it with the divine life-force that is clothed in the created beings to animate them,</t>
    <t s="13">that the created beings cover the divine life-force that is clothed within them.</t>
    <t s="14">And likewise with the divine power that brings the created beings into existence from nothing to something,</t>
    <t s="15">for the matter of nature within it is also from the term "immersion,"</t>
    <t s="16">since the bringing into existence is in a manner of concealment and hiding,</t>
    <t s="17">that the creative power is concealed and hidden within the created beings,</t>
    <t s="18">therefore the matter of "teva" from the term "immersion" and concealment applies to it.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="11">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section begins a new point, but is incomplete in the source.</sectionSummaryBrief>
